newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica garment exports register slight gain.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica garment exports register slight gain.

text.p: Jamaica's garment sector reported exports for the first six months of this year edged up one percent over last year, reversing the decline registered in 1996.

Total exports as of the end of June were US$258.8 million, up from US$254.7 million last year. Exports under the 807A program, under which garments are assembled for the U.S. market in the island's free zones, rose 8.1 percent and provided the bulk of the increase.

Last year, exports dropped 5.71 percent from US$581.6 million in 1995, to US$551.5 million. The Caribbean has lost some 123,000 apparel jobs to Mexico since the North American Free Trade Area came into being three years ago, and local officials blame last year's drop on this trend.
Garments are Jamaica's second-largest export earner, after bauxite and alumina.
